title: Punk photocopy flyer: one fluorescent ink, copier grain, ransom-note cut letters, spray-stencil numerals (esports broadcast)
summary: A single fluorescent pink is the only colour; everything else is black and paper white as if photocopied. Headlines are ransom notes (one scrap per character), codes and numbers are code-drawn stencil caps with two spray bridges, plates are torn strips of tape at small tilts, and photographs only appear as copier grain where there is no copy.

provenance.case: esports-broadcast v2 (北线联赛总决赛直播包装): scorebug (with an on-air composite and a 50% reflow), player card, ban/pick board, schedule poster and an 8 s opening; an original fictional league.
provenance.lineage: 1970s-80s punk and photocopy flyers (Jamie Reid's ransom-note lettering, Black Flag-style copier flyers): one fluoro ink, copier grain, cut letters, stencils. Borrowed: the grammar. Never borrowed: any flyer, sleeve, logo or lettering of theirs.
provenance.borrow: Borrow grammar, never assets. The copier ground is a public-domain painting (George Bellows, Stag at Sharkey's, 1909, Cleveland Museum of Art, CC0) processed into toner; the stencil letters are the bank's own code-drawn lettering.
provenance.rounds: v1 metro-map bracket (owner: 'too ordinary', the metro map is an esports cliché); v2 this pack. First pass: 13 tool findings, 10 by eye; final 0.
measured: Contrast: black on pink #FF2E88 6.6:1; paper white on pink about 2.5:1, so white text only ever sits on black plates.
64 px thumbnail against a generic dark UI kit: ban/pick 106 (v1 20) after the page became pink; the scorebug on air only 36 (a strip on gameplay stays small at 64 px: expected).
Ransom scraps must keep CJK fonts: a scrap that drew Barlow lost a glyph (北).

pink.use: the one ink: team A, the page ground of the board and poster; black text on it (6.6:1), never white text

black.use: plates, text on paper and pink, toner

paper.use: plates, team B's ink, text on black

grey.use: empty pips and banned glyphs (decoration only)

plate_dark.use: banned and picked hero tiles (paper text on it)

slate.use: the muted gameplay placeholder under the scorebug

num.use: Latin handles, dates, scores in tables, tracked subtitles; never a CJK scrap

fonts.resolve: fonts query --text "<copy>" --style gothic --weight 900 and --style mincho --weight 900 resolve Noto Sans SC and Noto Serif SC from the catalog; Barlow Condensed is Latin only (fonts measure --path <file>), and the layouts never give it a CJK scrap.
fonts.licence: All roles use SIL OFL 1.1 fonts.
fonts.lettering: Team codes, scores, timers and dates are the bank's code-drawn lettering (stencil 0, width 0.52, stroke 0.21, chamfer 0.05 all, slant -0.1) plus two spray bridges in the ground colour at 30% and 68% of the cap height, rotated -4 degrees.
fonts.note: Fonts are named, not bundled. --font-dir <dir> reads coverage and embeds the faces.

grammar: One ink only: fluorescent pink for one team, the page and the accents; everything else is black and paper as if photocopied.
Plates are strips of tape or torn paper, each at its own small tilt (-7 to +2 degrees) with one hard 5-6 px black shadow.
Headlines are ransom notes: one scrap per character, a seeded mix of black/paper/pink grounds and sans/serif faces, each tilted up to 6 degrees.
Numbers and codes are spray stencils at 1:10 or more against body text (a 236 px handle against 17 px).
Teams are told apart by code and position, never by colour alone (colour-blind viewers).
Photographs only as copier grain, and only where there is no copy: every line of text sits on a solid plate.

procedural: spray-stencil lettering (layouts-xerox.cjs stencil()): lettering.cjs caps with two bridges
ransom scraps (ransom()): seeded looks, one slot per character
stencil hero glyphs: twenty geometric marks cut by two bridges at -12 degrees
toner specks and copier streaks: the stand-in for a processed photograph
recipes: Copier ground: materials fetch --source cleveland --id 92937 --name bellows-stag; materials cut --file materials/raw/bellows-stag.png --mode none --finish ink; materials process --file materials/cut/bellows-stag/ink.png --effect photocopy --params '{"contrast":2.2,"threshold":0.5,"toner":0.0025,"streaks":0.5}' --seed 1, then tint it pink or keep it black and pass it to the xerox collage slot.
Paper for print: materials generate --generator paper --params '{"profile":"laid-cream"}' --seed 1, multiplied under paper plates only.
collage: The copier crowd is the only photograph: never under copy (collage-cover), cropped to bleed off the page edges.
materials.sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0) for the case's copier ground; any public-domain or owned photograph through the materials tools.

grammar: Cuts, not dissolves: at most five full-screen hard cuts in 8 s, never more than one a second (under the three-flash limit).
Ransom scraps slap on one by one (2-3 frames each) with a small overshoot; the copier ground pans slowly underneath.
The date drops in with a 2-frame shake; nothing fades, nothing glows.
Frames that only hold stencil paths are measured as lettering (data-kind=lettering or data-chk on the drawn group), not declared text-free.
motion.flashLimit: At most one full-screen ink change per second (pink/black hard cuts).

guidance: 64 px distinctiveness (guidance): the board and poster should read as 'pink copier flyer' at 64 px with the logo painted out; if pink falls under about half the screen (the v2 ban/pick was 10% before it became a pink page) the grammar is lost.
Measure fluorescent pink on the real stream chain before air: it shifts across screens and compression.
Spray bridges hide part of each glyph; they stay under the occlusion limit (15%) at two bars of 4.5% height.
checks.note: The browser check runs on every render: tilted scraps and plates overlap by design, so ink overlap and occlusion are measured.

examples.note: Screens of the case that stay example renders: see docs/cases/esports-broadcast/ (README showcase).
